clue.text: Tendency to criticise time-saving arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters of time-saving are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a scheme meant to save time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges the ten letters of TIME-SAVING; 'time-saving' reads as a describing word for the arrangement, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Negativism is a habitual sceptical or contrary attitude, a disposition to find fault.

clue.text: Fresh area of activity in the americas

parts.note: fresh means new
a world is a sphere or field of activity, as in 'the world of sport'

explanation.surface: A new field opens up for someone across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Americas were the lands Europeans discovered later, hence the common historical label for that hemisphere.

clue.text: One drives off when green's ahead

definitions.text: One drives off when green's ahead

parts.words: One drives off when green's ahead
parts.note: reads like a motorist pulling away when the traffic light turns green, but describes a sportsman hitting from the tee towards the putting surface

explanation.surface: A driver pulls away as the traffic light changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The traffic-light picture is the false trail: 'drives' is a long tee shot and 'green' the closely mown area round the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A player on a course drives the ball off the tee with the putting surface lying ahead.

clue.text: Take the first few small steps

definitions.text: Take the first few small steps

parts.words: Take the first few small steps
parts.note: sounds like making a tentative start on a project, but literally describes an infant beginning to walk

explanation.surface: Someone makes a cautious beginning on a new venture.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk unsteadily with short steps, as a very young child does when learning.

clue.text: Motor insurance acceptable in port

parts.note: a van is a motor vehicle

indicators.note: in puts the acceptable letter within the word for insurance

parts.note: insurance is cover
U means socially acceptable, upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A driver finds car insurance that will be accepted at the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: U for 'acceptable' comes from the old British distinction between U (upper-class) and non-U speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major Pacific seaport city in British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: Sailor had one dance

parts.note: a mariner is a sailor
a means one

explanation.surface: A seaman once enjoyed a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' only links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The marinera is a Peruvian couple dance performed with handkerchiefs.

clue.text: Partly stormy this traditional story

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A legend that is said to be somewhat stormy.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional tale, often explaining origins or involving gods and heroes.

clue.text: I jam coal violently into earthenware

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters of I jam coal are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone forcefully crams fuel into a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Majolica is a kind of tin-glazed decorated pottery, originally Italian.

clue.text: Solo item turned out to be arduous

indicators.note: turned out signals that the letters of solo item are rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A solo performance piece proved very hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilsome means laborious, requiring much hard effort.

clue.text: Words of praise are not rare

definitions.meaning: an exclamation congratulating someone on an achievement
describing steak or meat cooked thoroughly rather than pink

explanation.surface: Compliments are not so unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a congratulation and the term for meat cooked all the way through.

clue.text: Answer back with joanne in control

indicators.note: in places the short name within the word for control

parts.note: rein means control, as in keeping a tight rein
Jo is a short form of the name Joanne

explanation.surface: Someone retorts with a woman named Joanne in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoin is to reply sharply, to retort.

clue.text: Fail to notice what superintendents do

definitions.meaning: miss or neglect to see something
supervisors oversee and look over the work of others

explanation.surface: Supervisors are prone to missing things.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both missing something and, in an older sense, watching over or supervising.

clue.text: Bare minimum more presumably

parts.note: a phrase meaning 'at least that much' suggests a bare minimum, and if not fewer, then possibly greater

explanation.surface: A rough estimate: at least this, and perhaps more.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is used for emphasis, 'no fewer than', which sets a floor; anything beyond that floor is 'more'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase emphasises a minimum amount, implying the quantity is at least that, perhaps greater.

clue.text: Change direction, ever changing

indicators.note: changing tells us to alter the order of the letters of ever

explanation.surface: Someone forever altering course.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to swerve or turn suddenly onto a new course.

clue.text: Appear with Nancy (not north American) during crisis

parts.note: emerge means appear

indicators.note: not tells us to take the north and American letters out of the name Nancy

explanation.surface: A woman named Nancy turns up during an urgent situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not north American' strips N and A from NANCY, leaving NCY; 'with' and 'during' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous situation needing immediate action, a crisis.

clue.text: Fine weather

parts.note: reads as sunny conditions, but fine here means made of very small drops

explanation.surface: A pleasant sunny day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like 'pleasant', but it means 'in tiny particles': light rain in very small drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Drizzle is light rain falling in very small droplets.

clue.text: Call for military rising

parts.note: sounds like a demand for an armed uprising, but means a bugle signal waking soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone urges the army to revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' suggests a rebellion; it means getting out of bed in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle or drum signal sounded to wake soldiers at dawn.

clue.text: Clownishness of last character Annie performing on board

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: performing suggests Annie's letters are put through their paces in a new order

parts.note: SS is a steamship, the stock crossword ship: 'on board' a vessel puts that abbreviation in the answer

explanation.surface: A woman named Annie clowns around on a ship as the final act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' turns ANNIE into ANINE; 'on board' suggests a ship's deck but simply supplies the ship abbreviation SS, placed last.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaniness is comic silliness, the quality of a buffoon.

clue.text: Generosity of Scottish capital mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned says the phrase is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the capital or upper-case form of the opening letter of Scottish is a large S

explanation.surface: Edinburgh is noted for its generous spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish capital' suggests Edinburgh; it is the capital letter of 'Scottish', a large S, which said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or gifts.

clue.text: Fellow with peg protecting a larger aquatic mammal

indicators.note: protecting means the two words surround the article, keeping it safe inside

parts.note: man means fellow
a tee is a small peg on which a golf ball sits

explanation.surface: A man with a wooden leg shields a big sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'larger' is odd in the definition, but the manatee is indeed a large sea mammal; 'protecting' wraps the fellow-and-peg pair round A.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee, or sea cow, is a large plant-eating marine mammal.

clue.text: Sees red as a result of military order

parts.note: eyes means sees or looks at
red means left-wing in politics

explanation.surface: Someone becomes furious because of an army command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sees red' is the idiom for getting angry, which hides the split into two separate pieces; 'as a result of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On a parade ground, this command makes soldiers turn their heads to one side in salute.

clue.text: Learned about composer

indicators.note: about means the answer is surrounded by the outer letters of Learned, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Someone studied a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer, best known for 'Rule, Britannia!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was the English composer of 'Rule, Britannia!'.

clue.text: One lady or another going round women's institute

indicators.note: going round means one name surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: another lady, here Edna, a woman's name

explanation.surface: Two women walk around a meeting of a village club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute (WI) is a British community organisation for women, often in villages.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwina is a woman's given name, so it is one example of a lady's name.

clue.text: Leaves container for a cuppa

parts.note: sounds like someone walking out on a mug, but describes a pouch holding tea leaves

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a mug before making tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: tea leaves. A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small porous pouch holding tea leaves, used to brew a cup.

clue.text: Needlework in corner of large house?

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a corner of a map or compass
a wing is a section of a large building

explanation.surface: Embroidery done in a nook of a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the question mark flags the loose use of 'corner' for a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing means stitching with needle and thread, which is needlework.

clue.text: Old property

parts.note: sounds like an ancient building or estate, but means the quality of being elderly

explanation.surface: A historic building on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' suggests real estate; it means a quality or attribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Agedness is the state or quality of being elderly.

clue.text: Pincers be located in pairs

indicators.note: in places the word for being located inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PRS is the abbreviation for pairs
to lie is to be situated

explanation.surface: Gripping tools are found in twos.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are gripping tools with jaws, much like pincers.

clue.text: Practicable in Parisian style to begin with and desirable

indicators.note: to begin with means the French word comes at the start, ahead of the synonym

parts.note: en is French for in
viable means practicable or workable

explanation.surface: Something workable and attractive, done the French way from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Enviable describes something others would covet, highly desirable.

clue.text: Last character with Susan backing old Greek

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: backing means the short name for Susan is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Sue is a short form of Susan

explanation.surface: A woman named Susan supports an elderly Greek man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reads as supporting, but it is the reversal signal on the short name; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was the king of the gods in ancient Greek religion.

clue.text: Something it is not hard to miss

definitions.text: Something it is not hard to miss

parts.words: Something it is not hard to miss
parts.note: reads as something conspicuous, yet the real sense is a mark that is hard not to hit

explanation.surface: Something obvious that nobody could overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'not hard to miss' means conspicuous; literally it says the opposite of a thing you can hardly miss when aiming at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting duck, a mark so open to attack that hitting it is effortless.
